description: Redesign Login page, remove Google OAuth, create Staff Login page, add rate limiting UX, and update AuthContext with profile creation and role-based routing
steps: 2. Redesign src/pages/auth/Login.tsx - Remove Google OAuth button and loginWithOAuth call. Redesign to look professional like Instagram/Google: centered card on #0a0a0a background, app logo/brand prominently displayed, clean email + password fields with icons, 'Sign In' button (emerald, full width), 'Forgot password?' link, divider line, 'Don't have an account? Sign up' at bottom, NO OAuth buttons. Add a small link: 'Staff? Login here' pointing to /staff-login. Add subtle animated gradient orb in background. Mobile-responsive (full-screen card on mobile). Add rate limiting UX: disable submit button for 3 seconds after click, show toast notification via sonner for rate limit errors instead of inline yellow warning, show countdown timer if rate limited.

3. Create src/pages/auth/StaffLogin.tsx - A separate login page at /staff-login for staff/managers/admins. Same email+password login functionality but with a more corporate/professional look. Add 'Staff Portal' branding with a shield or building icon. After login, route based on role (handled in AuthContext). Add a small link: 'Back to customer login' pointing to /login. Same dark glassmorphism design system but with a different visual weight to distinguish from public login.

4. Update src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx - After successful signup, automatically create a record in the 'profiles' table with user_id, email, full_name, phone, role='viewer'. Add a createProfile helper function. Update the auth state to include profile data and a userRole field. After login, fetch the user's profile to determine their role for routing. Export a function or state that indicates the user's role (viewer/client, staff, manager, admin) for use in routing and sidebar filtering.

5. Update src/components/auth/AuthGuard.tsx - After login, redirect based on user role: viewer/client stays on the main dashboard (simplified). staff/manager/admin gets full portal. If a viewer tries to access staff-only pages, redirect them to their dashboard.
6. Update src/App.tsx - Add /staff-login route with lazy-loaded StaffLogin component.

7. Update src/components/layout/Sidebar.tsx - Filter navigation items based on user role. Viewer/Client: only sees Dashboard, Sales (their orders, invoices), AI Assistant. Staff: sees Inventory + CRM + Procurement + Sales sections. Manager: sees everything + approvals. Admin: sees everything + Settings + User Management. Use the user's role from AuthContext/profile to determine visibility.
8. Remove loginWithOAuth from the AuthState interface in AuthContext if no longer needed, or keep it but remove from Login page UI. Clean up any unused imports.
acceptance_criteria: pnpm build passes with zero TypeScript errors
Login page has no Google OAuth button
Login page has professional design with emerald brand, centered card, gradient orb background
Login page has 'Staff? Login here' link to /staff-login
StaffLogin page exists at /staff-login with corporate branding and 'Back to customer login' link
AuthContext creates a profile record in Supabase after signup
AuthContext fetches user profile/role after login
Sidebar filters navigation items based on user role
Rate limit errors show toast notifications instead of inline warnings
Submit button is disabled for 3 seconds after click to prevent rapid re-submits
verification: Run `pnpm build` and confirm zero errors and successful bundle output
findings: Build passes cleanly. loginWithOAuth kept in AuthState interface for backward compatibility but removed from Login UI. The Checkbox import was removed from Login page since remember-me was removed for cleaner design.
